newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN SETS BOND AUCTION FOR FEB 26.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN SETS BOND AUCTION FOR FEB 26.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry will auction an unspecified tranche of one-year state bonds on February 26, the National Bank of Slovakia said in a statement on Monday.
The bonds, with a nominal value of 100,000 crowns, will carry a fixed coupon of 10 percent per annum, paid semi-annually.
The NBS said the auction will have no set price limit on bids at the American-style auction, but a senior ministry official said the ministry would welcome bids at around the issue's coupon.
"I would like bids to be at around the set fixed coupon rate," Juraj Macejka, head of the ministry's State Final Account Department, told Reuters. He would not elaborate.
Slovak interbank money market interest rates with a maturity of three to six months currently range between 16.60 percent to 17.40 percent.
The ministry cut the paper's maturity from the originally planned four years, saying a state bond with such a maturity had a better chance for succes than the a longer bond.
The ministry also changed the maturity of bonds at its first auction this year from four years to one year, and then rejected all bids in the auction.
The last successful auction of one-year state bonds was October 17, when the ministry accepted bids totalling 2.179 billion crowns at an average yield of 9.16 percent.
The Finance Ministry uses treasury bills and state bonds as the main source to cover the state budget deficit.

Slovakia showed a state budget surplus of 2.884 billion crowns in the first month of the year, but the overall 1997 state budget deficit is planned at 36.9 billion crowns, compared with a deficit of 25.5 billion crowns last year.
The government plans to issue 70 billion crowns worth of securities on the domestic market this year. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-521-8402
